title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ANDRE'S TOWER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Andre Hollis, who mixes paint at the hardware store in Columbia, Mississippi.
He has mixed ten thousand gallons for other people. And he gets dizzy on a step stool.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN-UP SHEET
segments.quote: Don't be too timid and squeamish about your actions. All life is an experiment. The more experiments you make the better.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: The town water tower had faded to the color of old oatmeal.
The mayor wanted a volunteer painter. Andre's boss, Miss Odell, quoted Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Don't be too timid and squeamish about your actions. All life is an experiment. The more experiments you make the better.
So Andre signed up. Then he sat down, because his knees had heard the news.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: RUNG TWELVE
segments.quote: Look up and not down, look forward and not back, look out and not in, and lend a hand.
segments.author: Edward Everett Hale
lines: On Saturday he climbed the tower ladder. At rung twelve, he froze like a cat on a fence.
Walter, a retired lineman, called up the words of Edward Everett Hale:
Look up and not down, look forward and not back, look out and not in, and lend a hand.
Andre looked up. One rung. Then another. Walter climbed right behind him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE FIRST STRIPE
segments.quote: Art enables us to find ourselves and lose ourselves at the same time.
segments.author: Thomas Merton
lines: At the top, Andre planned every brushstroke and was too scared to make one.
Walter quoted the writer Thomas Merton:
Art enables us to find ourselves and lose ourselves at the same time.
So Andre stopped planning and painted one blue stripe. Then another.
He forgot the wind. He even forgot lunch, which for Andre was a first.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STORM
segments.quote: By perseverance the snail reached the ark.
segments.author: Charles Spurgeon
lines: Two weeks in, a Gulf storm washed half the fresh paint down the tower legs.
Walter shrugged and quoted the preacher Charles Spurgeon:
By perseverance the snail reached the ark.
So Andre went back up the next dry morning. Slow and steady. Snail speed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE COMMENTS
segments.quote: When a true genius appears in the world, you may know him by this sign, that the dunces are all in confederacy against him.
segments.author: Jonathan Swift
lines: Then the town's online group found the tower. Too blue. Too bright.
Miss Odell slid him a coffee and quoted the Irish writer Jonathan Swift:
When a true genius appears in the world, you may know him by this sign, that the dunces are all in confederacy against him.
Andre was pretty sure he was no genius. But he put his phone in a drawer and finished.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PORTRAIT
segments.quote: Every man's work, whether it be literature or music or pictures or architecture or anything else, is always a portrait of himself.
segments.author: Samuel Butler
lines: On the Fourth of July, the town gathered for the reveal: blue sky, the hardware store, and one tiny man on a ladder, waving.
His sister Renee quoted the English writer Samuel Butler:
Every man's work, whether it be literature or music or pictures or architecture or anything else, is always a portrait of himself.
Andre looked down at the crowd waving back, and he didn't feel dizzy at all.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Try it. Look up. Get lost in it. Keep going. Tune out the noise. Put yourself in it.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Try it. Look up. Get lost in it. Keep going. Tune out the noise. Put yourself in it.
I painted my own kitchen once. My wife calls it the incident.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
